official.description: The NTHU International Student Scholarship, funded by the Office of Global Affairs at National Tsing Hua University, is applied for through the same online system as admission to an NTHU international degree programme by selecting 'Apply for NTHU international student scholarship'. It provides a tuition and credit-fee waiver plus a tiered monthly stipend: NTD 20,000-40,000 per month for doctoral students, NTD 10,000 per month for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences or the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with supervisors from that college, and NTD 5,000 per month for master and bachelor students.
official.program_type: University scholarship for international degree students combining a full tuition and credit-fee waiver with a tiered monthly stipend
official.english_requirement: Proof of English Proficiency (not required for programmes fully taught in Chinese), fulfilling ONE of: a certificate of CEFR B2 level or above (TOEFL iBT 71, TOEIC 750, IELTS 5.5); a nationality document if from an English-speaking country (Philippines, Australia and New Zealand included; India not included); an official statement if the previous degree was fully taught in English; or a diploma if the previous degree was in an English language-related field. Departments may set higher scores than this minimum.

applicant_utility.summary: This award rides on your admission application, so the scholarship is effectively decided alongside admission - there is no separate form or portal. Doctoral applicants get the real money here (NT$20,000-40,000 a month plus a full tuition and credit-fee waiver), while bachelor's and master's applicants receive NT$5,000 a month plus the waiver, so at those levels treat the waiver as the main prize. Everything hinges on nationality status: you and both parents must hold only foreign nationality and have never held Taiwan nationality, and any earlier overseas-Chinese-student record in Taiwan disqualifies you. Budget for what the award ignores - dormitory, insurance, flights and daily living costs in Hsinchu.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strongest for PhD researchers, and for master's applicants whose main need is the tuition and credit-fee waiver; weakest value at bachelor's level beyond the waiver.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify every family member's nationality status first: you and your parents must all hold foreign nationality and have never held Taiwan nationality.
Shortlist programmes outside the excluded set (Medicine, Dentistry, Traditional Chinese Medicine at undergraduate level, the College of Semiconductor, and ICDF programmes) before drafting anything.
Apply inside the intake window (the published Spring 2027 window ran 3 August - 30 September 2026, 15:00 Taiwan time) and tick 'Apply for NTHU international student scholarship' in the portal.
Arrange a bank financial statement issued within the last 3 months showing more than USD 4,000 equivalent, or attach proof of an already-awarded scholarship, unless you are an ICDF applicant.
Brief recommenders early: letters must be submitted by the recommender through NTHU's online recommendation system and are rejected if you upload them yourself.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 15:00 Taiwan-time cut-off on deadline day or leaving one upload slot empty - late or incomplete applications are not considered at all.
Assuming full funding: the award waives tuition and credit fees only, and the bachelor's/master's stipend is just NT$5,000 per month.
Holding an ICDF award or any government scholarship, which blocks this scholarship on ICDF programmes and limits it to a non-ICDF programme if you are admitted to both.
Applying to a Chinese-taught programme without checking that department's actual language-proficiency requirement, which can exceed the minimum.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dormitory rent, student insurance, international flights and daily living costs are not covered. For scale, NTHU's published international graduate tuition is TWD 26,300-36,300 per semester (about USD 797-1,100) plus per-credit fees of TWD 1,580-2,100, so the waiver is worth roughly USD 1,600-2,200 per year at graduate level; undergraduate international tuition is TWD 46,100-53,200 per semester.
document_audit: Multi-page documents must be merged into a single PDF per document category, with a 5 MB maximum per file.

The financial certificate must clearly show the account holder's name, issue date, currency and balance, and be issued within 3 months - a sponsor who is not you also needs the signed Certification of Financial Responsibility form.

English or Mandarin proofs must be one of the exact listed document types (certificate, nationality document, official statement of medium of instruction, or diploma); a self-written description is explicitly refused.
Recommendation letters count only if the recommender submits them through the online system before the deadline - paper copies are not accepted and you cannot upload them.
alerts: The Spring 2027 window has already closed; watch the international admission news page for the next intake instead of assuming a rolling deadline.
Scholarship results are published separately from admission results (late December for Spring 2027), so an offer does not guarantee the stipend tier you are counting on.

Doctoral awards are tiered: Humanities and Social Sciences PhD students (and Intercollegiate PhD students supervised from that college) receive NT$10,000 rather than the NT$20,000-40,000 given to other PhD students.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission in NTHU's International Student Online Application System covers both admission and the scholarship; tick the scholarship option, upload every document before the 15:00 Taiwan-time deadline, then await the separate scholarship announcement in late December.

The only recurring dates are the per-semester deadlines by which existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts to remain eligible for the following semester. applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this one - it finds you. NYCU awards it through your college's nomination and a scholarship committee review, so the practical move is to build the academic record and advisor relationships that make a nomination likely during doctoral admission. If you win, the money is real: NT$33,000 a month for two years plus a tuition waiver, comfortably covering living costs in Hsinchu, but basic incidental fees such as dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees still come out of your pocket. Holding any Taiwan government scholarship or grant disqualifies you, and this award is mutually exclusive with the general NYCU International Student Scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-performing incoming doctoral students at NYCU whose college is willing to nominate them and who hold no other Taiwan government funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up a PhD supervisor and college backing early - nomination runs through the college, so make yourself known to the department before admission decisions are made.

Confirm you hold no scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government (including Taiwan Scholarship, ESP, UST, TIGP, NSNT, ICDF or the general NYCU International Student Scholarship), as these are treated as government-funded and mutually exclusive.
Keep your academic record strong through admission, since the award targets new Ph.D. students with outstanding grades.
If awarded, diarise the per-semester deadline for transcripts and tuition payment receipts - missing it costs eligibility for the following semester.
Plan at least 2 Mandarin courses into your study plan, as recipients must enroll in them during their studies.
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can apply - there is no student application form, so waiting for a window means missing the award entirely.
Holding a Taiwan government scholarship or grant, which NYCU treats as disqualifying both for this award and for the general NYCU International Student Scholarship.
Failing to submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before the per-semester deadline, which voids next-semester eligibility.
Budgeting only for tuition and forgetting dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees, which the waiver does not touch.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Dormitory, insurance, campus facility and other incidental fees remain payable; living costs beyond the NT$33,000 monthly stipend, plus international flights and settling-in costs, are on the student. Note the stipend is in principle paid on the 10th of each month, except January and the start of each semester (September), so plan cash flow for those gaps.
document_audit: Every semester you must file both the transcript and the tuition payment receipt - one without the other is an incomplete submission.
Watch the per-semester cut-off announced by the OIA: this renewal paperwork is the only recurring administration the award has, and it is what keeps next semester's money flowing.

There is no admission-stage document package for this award - nomination paperwork sits with the college and the scholarship committee, so ask your prospective department what it needs from you to support a nomination.
alerts: This is nomination-only: nothing you submit directly produces an application, and the windows on the OIA scholarship system (e.g. Spring 2027 New Students Scholarship, 10 August - 13 November 2026) do not cover this award.
The stipend and waiver run for 2 years only; years 3 onward of the PhD depend on other funding such as NSTC or advisor-supported schemes.

If your college does not nominate you, the general NYCU International Student Scholarship is the fallback worth applying for in its published windows (Fall: 15 January - 15 March; Spring: 15 July - 15 September for current students, or alongside admission for incoming students).
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No student submission exists: the college nominates, the scholarship committee reviews, and recipients then file transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester to keep the award.
